A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same layer-swapping study. Their main text, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Llama 3.1 fine-tuning and model-merging experiments, including MGSM comparisons in Tables 1–2, parameter analyses, and appendix souping results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports detailed performance of the selected experts in Appendix A.3, Table 5.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same layer-selection rules, transition-zone averaging, and configurations. Renaming averaging weights from w to alpha and adding algorithm comments do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: The four target languages, English math training, and SFT datasets in Table 3 are unchanged. MGSM, BELEBELE, FLORES, MBPP, and MMLU were already used in v1; v2's expert-performance table supplies results within that existing coverage.

E2.justification: The base model, individual language and math experts, and model-soup comparisons remain unchanged. The Swahili comparison still includes TIES-merging and joint SFT, and the appendix retains the same souping combinations.

E3.justification: The model size, training budgets, expert selection, nine-pair comparisons, MGSM 8-shot evaluation, and Table 4 hyperparameters are unchanged. The metrics and shot counts newly specified in Table 5 document previously described evaluations rather than establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the sparsification investigations, layer-configuration and transition-zone analyses, parameter heatmaps, and combinations with souping. V1's Table 5 becomes v2's Table 6 without changed results. The added expert benchmark scores do not introduce a new ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions describe different sampling seeds across training runs and aggregate results over three selected experts or nine merged pairs. V2's additional expert averages follow this existing practice; no new repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: V2 Table 5 adds detailed selected-expert scores, especially for BELEBELE, FLORES, MBPP, and MMLU, extending supporting numerical evidence. Tables 1–2 and v1 Table 5/v2 Table 6 are unchanged. The new table also reports a base-model MGSM aggregate of 0.311 without explaining its difference from Table 2's 37.7%.

T1.justification: The fine-tuning delta and mean-absolute-value definitions and merging arithmetic are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added; the new English-representation explanation is interpretive.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same contribution: inexpensive post hoc composition of language and math experts for cross-lingual transfer. The claimed comparative advantage and proposed broader applicability are not substantively revised.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains success through English-centric internal representations and multilingual mappings in the outer layers. Section 7 reframes pretraining dependence around this explanation and removes the explicit weaker-model example. Section 6 also drops speculation connecting update magnitudes to original weight size and proximity to the output.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 explicitly identifies next-token prediction as the SFT objective. New Table 5 specifies benchmark metrics and prompting details, including 5-shot accuracy for BELEBELE/MMLU and 0-shot evaluation for FLORES/MBPP. Table 4 clarifies that warmup values denote steps; its numerical hyperparameters and the dataset access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references, including Wendler, Alabi, Kojima, and Aakanksha, strengthening connections to latent-language research and multilingual model merging. The Devlin et al. BERT reference is removed. PLUG's change from a 2023 preprint to a 2024 publication is an update to the same work.

P1.justification: V2 makes local grammatical corrections and explanatory refinements throughout, adds comments to Algorithm 1, reorders a discussion paragraph, and inserts the individual-expert appendix subsection. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 5 and reformats Figure 2 with clearer attention and feed-forward column labels while retaining its values. Figure 3 and Tables 1–2 are relocated, and conference headers are added. The existing appendix heatmaps and souping table are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.3 makes the previously qualitative account of expert performance more inspectable, while explicit metrics, prompting details, and clearer Figure 2 labels improve transparency and readability. The benefit is limited by the new table's unexplained MGSM aggregate discrepancy and the absence of additional merged-model validation. Overall, these are modest improvements to documentation rather than stronger evidence for the central method.
